main_body: East-facing pew with wooden backrest on the left (rows 8-46) and seat with red cushions on the right (rows 13-46).
top_band: Seat surface seen from above (rows 13-41) with red cushions (rows 16-26 and 29-39) on wooden seat frame.
evidence: This is an east-facing pew (3 tiles tall). Reading a vertical column through the seat (e.g. col 9): row 13 is the back outline, rows 14-41 form the horizontal seat surface seen from above (wood frame with two red seat cushions at rows 16-26 and 29-39), row 42 is a lighter wood front-edge highlight line, and rows 43-45 are the vertical south-facing side/front apron of the seat base, with row 46 as the bottom shadow. The backrest on the left rises above the seat (rows 8-40) with its south face at rows 41-45.

style.evidence: The candidate has large completely flat fills: the two 5x10 red cushion rectangles are 100% single-colour red with only a 1px dark shadow on bottom/right, and the backrest is a uniform vertical strip of 2 flat browns with zero wood grain or variation. Compared to the Beodeul references which have rich wood grain, specular highlights, and 5-6 shading steps, this piece is geometric and flat.
